cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Did the boss calling us office furniture hurt you? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? Are you making a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. It's still in drafts. How did you feel?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. Mine says 'unprofessional'; I'm changing that to 'I went home and cried.'

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 withholds A feelings until B4; A5 reveals matching hurt through draft wording, but A3 rank/adjustment claim is not enacted.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 complaint concern is answered with draft status; B4 invisible feeling can motivate A5 more personal wording.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to know how the admission will be used and B4 names the injury after long service.

heightening.evidence: B4 emotional admission causes A5 to replace professional complaint language with shared tears.

specificity.evidence: A1 boss insult and B4 twelve years establish workplace hurt without more history.
